corrections: Replaced the shared twin-radial prototype with a dedicated low-cabin D18S airframe, tapered six-degree outer wings, rounded twin fins, two exposed nine-cylinder R985s, short streamlined nacelles, retractable gear and two-blade propellers.

Exterior overlays corrected wing and cockpit stations, fuselage height, cowling position, excessive nacelle length and tail shape. Final independent views caught and corrected an escaping rear floor and a roof-intersecting overhead radio.

N522B cockpit has a measured-width shaped panel, raised four-radio block, separate left/right flight clusters, dual independent engine RPM needles, bow-tie wheels, six-lever quadrant, sloping subpanels, pedals, fans, overhead radio and six passenger seats.

Simulation sources drive TAS in mph, geometric altitude, true heading, attitude, vertical speed, yaw rate, each engine RPM, flaps, gear, throttles, wheels and pedals. Differential aileron travel and elevator limits follow Beech Specification131.
Texture-free polygonal geometry, true window apertures, material-batched detail and unchanged lazy asset loading.
reviewNotes.visual: Personally compared all four final overlays, all eight standard views and twelve detail/state views: zero, cruise, limits, below-sea-level, missing telemetry, gear-up, positive/negative controls, overhead, quadrant, cabin and close exterior. Final captures match source hash; repeated after floor/roof corrections.
limitations: Exterior three-view is Art Mills/Paul Matt drawing6-59-A of a postwar-modified1940 Model18, not an exact D18S blueprint. Beech D18S numeric dimensions take precedence; small residual outline differences and clipped opposite wing/tail edges are documented.

The N522B cockpit photograph is perspective and partially occluded. Panel scale uses the45.75in width in the D18S trainer specification, while civilian instruments differ. Control-depth and eye coordinates remain estimates, not surveyed ergonomics.

Static12.283-degree tailwheel stance is baked into geometry and rigidly removed for drawing comparisons. The simplified simulation does not articulate the fuselage from ground stance into a separate flight datum. The operator eye is high/forward to preserve the horizontal sightline.

RPM converts each normalized engine state to2300rpm; this is the simulation abstraction, not a complete piston-engine/governor model. Speed is explicitly TAS, altitude geometric and heading true. Manifold pressure, oil, fuel, temperature, navigation, clock, mixture and prop-governor indications are unavailable and remain unanimated/blank.
Rivets, fabric ribs and radio faces are selective geometric details. No reference photograph or drawing pixels are embedded. Paint is an original ivory/blue scheme, not N522B livery.
